speaker: Doctor
text: That is a concerning combination of symptoms. To determine if this is neuromuscular or neurological in origin, can you tell me if your double vision worsens when you close one of your eyes?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detail; the fluctuating weakness and specific eye movement triggers strongly suggest a myasthenic process. To confirm this, I need to see your strength and reflexes objectively. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Neurological_Exam including Grip_Strength and Deep_Tendon_Reflexes.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Grip Strength: Diminished in bilateral upper extremities. Deep Tendon Reflexes: Normal throughout all extremities. Additional Findings: Ptosis present in the right upper eyelid, worsening with sustained upward gaze; diminished motor strength in upper extremities with normal tone and no obvious atrophy.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.
